title: Difference as mercy
hook: a well-known saying calls scholarly difference a mercy

segments.voice: Yesterday, taqlid, and your line: follow one who knows. Whose knowledge did you lean on, and why do you trust them? Day one thousand one hundred eighty.

An instruction goes out to a company of the Prophet's companions: none of you is to pray the afternoon prayer except at the settlement of Banu Qurayza. They set off. The sun drops lower on the road. Now there's a problem. If they keep walking, the prayer's time will pass. One group says: he meant hurry, not miss the prayer, and they stop and pray on the road. Another group says: he said there, and they pray only when they arrive, late. Same words, two honest readings. In Sahih al-Bukhari, when the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, hears about it, he blames neither group. Today's word is what happened on that road.
screen: `PRAY ONLY AT BANU QURAYZA.` → `THE SUN SINKS ON THE ROAD.` → `TWO READINGS, NEITHER BLAMED.`

segments.voice: The word is ikhtilaf, difference, disagreement, the scholars going different ways. There's a saying people repeat: the difference of my community is a mercy. It's quoted as a hadith, and here honesty matters. Hadith scholars have said they found no reliable chain for it back to the Prophet. The idea, though, is carried by other reports. A saying attributed to the caliph Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz has him say he would not have been glad if the companions had never differed, because their difference left room for those who came after. And a story the biographies tell: a caliph wanted to make Imam Malik's book, al-Muwatta, the single law for every city. Malik declined. The companions had spread to different cities, he said, each carrying what they knew, and people should be left with what had reached them. Think back to the road. The words were the same; the readings differed; both were honest; neither was blamed. That's the picture of a mercy. Two schools can place the hands differently in prayer, and both be following their method faithfully. But this is not difference about everything. It lives inside a shared ground: the oneness of God, the prayer, the fast, the Qur'an. And it's difference reached by method, the method of the last two weeks. This closes the foundations: shari'ah and fiqh, the Qur'an and sunnah, agreement, analogy, reason, the common good, custom, the five rulings, the wide permitted, striving, following. And now difference, held as mercy. Next, the schools themselves, one by one, beginning with the merchant of Kufa.
screen: `IKHTILAF: GOING DIFFERENT WAYS.` · `A SAYING WITH NO SOUND CHAIN.` · `MALIK WON'T MAKE ONE LAW.` · `DIFFERENCE INSIDE SHARED GROUND.`

segments.voice: The practice: respect a different ruling. Bring to mind a way someone else practices that isn't yours. Some Muslims pray with arms folded, and others with arms at their sides, each following their school. Or something closer to home, a family that keeps a holiday differently from yours. Hold it without correcting it. Ask: what honest reading might be behind this? Like the group on the road who prayed late, and the group who didn't. If you pray, you can pray for the person who differs from you. If not, hold them kindly until the bell. The bell holds the time.
Ikhtilaf. Difference among scholars, reached by honest method, held as a mercy. Today's word.
Your line: difference, mercy. Today, when someone reads the same words differently, look for the honest reading before you look for the error. Day one thousand one hundred eighty.

howItsDone: Muslims of different schools pray and fast according to their own school's rulings side by side in the same mosques, and scholars study the reasons behind each school's view in a field called the study of disagreement.

fork.setup: you're on the road to Banu Qurayza. you were told to pray the afternoon prayer only there, and the sun is setting. what do you do?
options: pray on the road, reading the order as 'hurry'.
pray only on arrival, reading the order as 'there'.
either: both groups did, and neither was blamed.
fork.reveal: one group prayed on the road, the other on arrival. the Prophet blamed neither. two honest readings of the same words.

original.note: Arabic: difference, disagreement; going different ways.

trapdoor: what you thought: disagreement among scholars is a failure to find the answer.
what it means: honest difference, reached by method, inside a shared ground, held as a mercy.
what a scholar hears: the famous saying has no sound chain; the road to Banu Qurayza and Malik's refusal carry the idea instead.

notes: Bukhari 946: confirm number and paraphrase (Muslim 1770 has the noon prayer in its version).
Status of 'ikhtilafu ummati rahmah': hadith scholars (e.g., al-Subki, al-Albani) said no reliable chain is known; confirm framing.
Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's reported saying: confirm attribution and source.
Malik and the caliph (variously al-Mansur or Harun al-Rashid) over al-Muwatta: told as 'a story the biographies tell'; confirm.
Examples of difference: arms folded vs at the sides in prayer (e.g., Maliki and Ja'fari practice of sadl): confirm fair and accurate.
Part close: names the Foundations part's words (days 1168–1180) and points to the Hanafi school (day 1181).
